title: A finite subset of a Galois extension lies in a finite Galois subextension
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $\Omega/k$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension] which is Galois: separable algebraic [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension] and normal (for every $\alpha\in\Omega$ the minimal polynomial of $\alpha$ over $k$ is a product of polynomials of degree one in $\Omega[T]$). Let $S\subseteq\Omega$ be a finite subset. Then there is a subfield $M$ with $k\subseteq M\subseteq\Omega$ and $S\subseteq M$ such that $M/k$ is finite ($\dim_kM<\infty$), separable algebraic, and normal (for every $\beta\in M$ the minimal polynomial of $\beta$ over $k$ is a product of polynomials of degree one in $M[T]$); i.e. $M/k$ is finite Galois (Stacks, Fields, Definition 09I0). One may take for $M$ the normal closure over $k$ of $k(S)$ inside $\Omega$.
